This file is the **iter-193 Pic0AbelianVariety** file-skeleton (NEW lane,
blueprint-doctor flagged orphan resolution for the iter-192 plan-phase chapter
`Picard_Pic0AbelianVariety.tex`). It packages the strategy phase A.3.iii–vi
substrate and the A.3.vii assembly into the load-bearing Route~A statement
`Pic⁰_{C/k}` is an abelian variety, the gate of `thm:nonempty_jacobianWitness`
for `g(C) ≥ 1` curves.

The chapter consumes the abstract identity-component substrate set up in
`Picard/IdentityComponent.lean` (`Pic⁰_{C/k}` as a clopen subgroup scheme of
finite type, geometrically irreducible, formation commuting with base change)
and adds the curve-specific input: the tangent-space isomorphism
`T₀ Pic⁰_{C/k} ≅ H¹(C, 𝒪_C)`, the resulting smoothness of dimension `g` at
the origin (hence everywhere by translation), properness inherited from the
projectivity of `Pic⁰_{C/k}` for `C/k` geometrically normal, and the assembly
into an abelian variety in the sense of Milne §I.1.

structure, via `IdentityComponent.isSubgroupHomomorphism` +
`PicScheme.groupSchemeStructure`), `tangentSpaceCotangentDual`,

`isFiniteTypeGeometricallyIrreducible`, whose QC∧GeomIrred conjuncts were
closed in run 0009 — `IdentityComponent.lean`, Kleiman §5 Lem.~`lem:agps`(3)),
the `isAbelianVariety` assembly, and the moved
`Pic0Scheme.isAbelianVariety` (blueprint pin `thm:pic_zero_is_abelian_variety`).

# FGA representability of the Picard scheme

This file states the FGA representability of the relative Picard functor of a
smooth proper geometrically integral curve `C/k`, following Kleiman, "The
Picard scheme", §2 and §4 (cf. FGA Explained Ch. 9; arXiv:math/0504020).

The relative Picard functor is

```
picSharp C := PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ forget AddCommGrpCat
```

the set-valued shadow of the `H_T`-coset carrier
`T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` of `Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean` (Kleiman §2
Def. `df:Pfs`; blueprint `def:rel_pic_sharp`). A `RepresentableBy` witness
against it is a natural bijection
`(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`, which is what the downstream
tangent-space computation (`AJC.pic0av`, `Pic0.tangentSpaceIso`) attaches to.

## The étale-sheafification route (owner decision of 2026-07-28)

Kleiman §4 represents the **étale-sheafified** functor `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, and
that is what this file's obligation is stated against —
`fgaPicardRepresentability`, over an **arbitrary** base field, with **no
hypothesis on `C(k)`**. The functor is built and its sheaf property proved in
`Picard/PicEtSheaf.lean` (`PicScheme.picEt`, `picEt_isSheaf_forget`), by
sheafifying the relative Picard presheaf for Mathlib's big étale topology
localised at `Spec k`.

Why the sheafification is not optional. The plain relative functor
`picSharp C = T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` is not representable over a
general field, so an unconditional `RepresentableBy` against `picSharp` is a
**false** statement, not merely an unproved one.

/-!
# Projectivity of smooth proper curves

A finite morphism to the projective line supplies finite Laurent two-chart
data, hence a closed immersion into a relative projective space.  The existing
nonconstant-map construction produces that finite morphism under exactly the
ambient hypotheses of the algebraic Jacobian challenge.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

noncomputable section

universe u

open CategoryTheory AlgebraicGeometry

namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic

variable {k : Type u} [Field k]

/-- A proper scheme admitting a finite morphism to the projective line is
projective over the base field. -/
theorem isProjective_of_hasFiniteMapToP1
    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    [IsProper C.hom] [HasFiniteMapToP1 C] : C.hom.IsProjective := by
  obtain ⟨pi, hpi⟩ := HasFiniteMapToP1.nonempty_finite_map (C := C)
  letI : IsFinite pi.left := hpi
  exact (p1LaurentChartData k).isProjective_of_finiteMap pi

/-- A smooth proper geometrically integral relative curve is projective over
the base field. -/
theorem isProjective_of_smoothProperGeometricallyIntegral
    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] : C.hom.IsProjective := by
  haveI : HasFiniteMapToP1 C := inferInstance
  exact isProjective_of_hasFiniteMapToP1 C

/-- At the scheme universe supported by `IsProjectiveWith`, a smooth proper
geometrically integral relative curve carries a relatively very ample line
bundle, with no hypothesis beyond the curve's own. -/
theorem exists_isProjectiveWith_of_smoothProperGeometricallyIntegral
    {k₀ : Type} [Field k₀] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] :
    ∃ L : C.left.Modules, C.hom.IsProjectiveWith L :=
  (isProjective_of_smoothProperGeometricallyIntegral C).exists_isProjectiveWith

/-- Projectivity under exactly the smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible
curve hypotheses used by the algebraic Jacobian challenge. -/
theorem isProjective_of_smoothProperGeometricallyIrreducible
    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] : C.hom.IsProjective := by
  letI : GeometricallyIntegral C.hom :=
    SmoothOfRelativeDimension.geometricallyIntegral 1 C.hom
  exact isProjective_of_smoothProperGeometricallyIntegral C

id: AJC.picrep.quasiprojective
title: 'Quasi-projectivity vocabulary: graded prime avoidance => FiniteInAffine, and
  the seam antecedent in standard terms'
projects:
- Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge
summary: "LANDED sorry-free by pic-e (0095 r7). The seam sorry fgaPicardRepresentability\
  \ is UNTOUCHED and rep still has no producer.\n\nPicard/QuasiProjectiveFiniteInAffine.lean,\
  \ rooted at AlgebraicJacobian.lean, 14 declarations (COUNTED BY KEYWORD -- 13 theorems\
  \ + 1 def; the one grep hit for 'sorry' is docstring prose), ZERO code sorries,\
  \ ALL 13 theorems axiom-clean [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] against fgaPicardRepresentability\
  \ firing sorryAx in the SAME probe. lake build AlgebraicJacobian EXIT=0, 8918 jobs,\
  \ zero warnings from this file. Commits 7a29218a49, fb36b34c67, e445e72358, 128dfd81ef,\
  \ 49b712d5ca.\n\nWHAT WAS MISSING AND IS NOW BUILT. Three files said the same sentence\
  \ -- 'holds for quasi-projective X, but mathlib v4.31 has no quasi-projectivity\
  \ vocabulary at this pin, so it must be supplied by hand' (PicEtPointedReduction.lean,\
  \ Albanese/StableAffineCoverGroup.lean, FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean). Nobody built\
  \ it. Of the whole chain exactly ONE step has content and it IS absent from mathlib:\
  \ GRADED prime avoidance. The ungraded Ideal.subset_union_prime_finite gives an\
  \ element with no degree control, and Proj.isAffineOpen_basicOpen demands f in A_m\
  \ with 0 < m.\n\n * exists_homogeneous_pos_mem_notMem -- one relevant homogeneous\
  \ prime. The grading is consumed TWICE and the second use is the one an ungraded\
  \ reading drops: homogeneity of I gives a homogeneous element outside p with NO\
  \ degree control; RELEVANCE of p supplies the positive degree, because a witness\
  \ in the irrelevant ideal has zero degree-0 component. FALSE at a p containing the\
  \ irrelevant ideal -- exactly the primes Proj discards -- so relevance is load-bearing.\n\
  \ * exists_homogeneous_pos_mem_forall_notMem_of_antichain / _forall_notMem -- the\
  \ finite family, by the product/sum trick with degrees equalised via M := prod of\
  \ degrees and F q := f q ^ (M / m q). The general form reduces to the MAXIMAL members:\
  \ avoiding a maximal prime avoids everything below, so the ungraded reflex of reducing\
  \ to MINIMAL primes would prove nothing here.\n * finiteInAffine_proj -- the geometric\
  \ half, and the hypotheses line up for free: a point of Proj IS a relevant homogeneous\
  \ prime, and its structure field not_irrelevant_le does DOUBLE duty as the relevance\
  \ input and (with I := the irrelevant ideal) as the 'I not below p' input. Mathlib\
  \ runs this one point at a time inside Proj's own local_affine field; this is its\
  \ finite generalisation.\n * finiteInAffine_of_isAffineHom / _projectiveSpace /\
  \ _of_isProjective -- transport. Generalises the landed finiteInAffine_left_of_isAffineHom,\
  \ whose Y = Spec k case concludes from the source being AFFINE; here Y need only\
  \ satisfy FiniteInAffine, and P(n;S) does without being affine.\n\nWHAT IS ACTUALLY\
  \ DISCHARGED: orbitsInAffineOpen_of_isProjective closes the Galois-descent engine's\
  \ orbit gate at EVERY projective scheme, no affineness, nothing supplied by hand.\
  \ Prior producers were the affine total space (no room to be false) and a base-change\
  \ transport. finiteInAffine_curve gives the curve unconditionally via isProjective_of_smoothProperGeometricallyIntegral.\n\
  \nWHAT IS NOT, and it is in the source not only here: the FiniteInAffine conjunct\
  \ of PointedPicSharpRep is about the PICARD scheme, and nothing in-tree produces\
  \ projectivity of a Picard scheme (Kleiman th:qpp&p, open). §5 restates the antecedent\
  \ AS projectivity (PointedPicSharpRepProjective) and carries it to the seam (fgaPicardRepresentability_of_projective),\
  \ so a lane proving that closes the sorry by exact. THE OBLIGATION DID NOT SHRINK\
  \ -- same mathematics, hypothesis named the way the source names it. What it removes\
  \ is 'is FiniteInAffine the right hypothesis or a formalisation artefact?': it is\
  \ a CONSEQUENCE of the right one.\n\nBOTH VACUITY HALVES MEASURED: isProjective_id_spec\
  \ lands Spec k projective over itself (satisfiable); exact? FAILS on X.hom.IsProjective\
  \ for arbitrary X with [LocallyOfFiniteType] (not free); and the new antecedent\
  \ does NOT close hypothesis-free. CONVERSE NOT CLAIMED: FiniteInAffine does not\
  \ obviously recover a closed immersion, so 'strictly stronger' is unmeasured."

id: AJC.picrep.projectivity
title: Smooth proper curves over a field are projective
projects:
- Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge
summary: Closed without new hypotheses. Arbitrary relative projective coordinate charts
  are identified with affine space; the two normalized chart factors are closed immersions;
  their target opens have exact preimages equal to the pulled-back Laurent charts
  and cover the global map's range; target-locality gives an immersion, and properness
  gives projectivity. The rooted theorem isProjective_of_smoothProperGeometricallyIrreducible
  uses exactly the AJC smooth/proper/geometrically irreducible binders.
